about: Interactions about work items in two orchestrator conversations and five repo sessions (and their subagents) over 2026-03-12/16, anonymized and moved to a fictional domain (acme's invoice exporter). Counts are occurrences in that window. 'protocol' is how the ledger protocol handles the pattern now; 'replay' and 'guard' name the scenarios (replay/*.json) and real commands (orchestrator_commands.json) that check it.

patterns.name: delegation through bosun delegate
patterns.detail: fix-my-pr 4, review 3, investigate 2, new-work 1; all to windows already running Claude; 6 with --details on a quoted heredoc
patterns.example: bosun delegate new-work --id 'slack:C0000000003/1700000035.000035' --requester 'Marco Rossi' --ask '...' --window exporter-tax --details - <<'EOF' ... EOF
patterns.protocol: unchanged, and the ledger now records the window on each item once the task is delivered

patterns.name: hand-written task over raw bosun send (before delegate existed)
patterns.detail: 2 with send --new (day 1 06:39), 2 to a running window (day 1 09:01, 10:01); all carried 'Ledger id:' in the text
patterns.example: bosun send exporter-tax "Ledger id: mypr:acme/exporter#102\nPR: ...\nAsk: address the 4 unresolved CodeQL review threads ..."
patterns.protocol: the guard denies the orchestrator's send without --id/--no-item and send --new; tasks go through delegate

patterns.name: addendum to a task already delegated
patterns.detail: orchestrator: 1 over raw send (day 2 06:07, the '-' incident) and 1 as a whole second delegate ('Follow-up to the earlier fix task', day 2 06:03); me: 1 through my other session without an id ('Update from the user on how to finish this task', day 1 07:12) and 2 typed into windows ('make sure the PRs are not approved or merged yet'), which interrupted running review subagents
patterns.example: bosun send exporter-tax 'Addendum to the queued payment-terms task (slack:C0000000003/1700000035.000035). ...'
patterns.protocol: bosun delegate --update <id> --details -: goes to the recorded window, framed 'Update to ledger item <id>', kept in history, refused for items never delegated or finished; a second whole hand-over of an item that has not reported is refused, pointing to --update, unless --again

patterns.name: free-text correction of an earlier message
patterns.detail: orchestrator: 'Ignore the "-" message just sent' (day 2 06:08); me to the orchestrator: 'Wrong window, ignore last message' (day 2 06:10)
patterns.example: bosun send exporter-tax 'Ignore the "-" message just sent, that was a mistake. Addendum ...'
patterns.protocol: send no longer pastes '-', and the guard denies the orchestrator's free-text send; corrections go through delegate --update

patterns.name: literal '-' pasted into a repo session
patterns.detail: `send <window> -` with a heredoc: send did not read stdin; the session answered with a status line
patterns.example: bosun send exporter-tax - 2>/dev/null <<'EOF' || bosun send exporter-tax '...'
patterns.protocol: '-' reads stdin; an empty stdin is refused

patterns.name: outcome reported as a free-text ledger note
patterns.detail: notes of 26-1063 characters (median about 400): commits, PR URLs, report paths, open questions and decisions needed, all in one string
patterns.example: bosun ledger note 'mypr:acme/exporter#104' 'Pushed 3 commits (CI green). Answered all 6 threads ... OPEN: ... Needs a decision ...'
patterns.protocol: bosun ledger report <id> --summary <one line> --result <URL or path> --open <what is left> [--state]; notes still work for tasks handed over earlier

patterns.name: state transitions by repo sessions
patterns.detail: prepared 1, reviewed 3 (one already reviewed: 'unchanged'), 1 refused: a guessed state 'posted'
patterns.protocol: report --state makes the same validated transition with the outcome; the refusal lists the allowed states

patterns.name: field update that needed --kind
patterns.detail: 2 orchestrator upserts without --kind (day 1 11:01) and 1 repo-session upsert with a wrong kind name ('review')
patterns.protocol: upsert updates an existing item without --kind; a wrong kind is still refused

patterns.name: orchestrator reads a window's screen to learn an outcome
patterns.detail: tmux capture-pane on 4 occasions: an investigation's answer (for a draft reply I asked for), two reviews that recorded nothing, a queued task's status, and to check the '-' delivery
patterns.protocol: ledger reports and list (@window, awaiting report|reported); policy: no screen reading, ask with delegate --update

patterns.name: orchestrator greps notes to find outcomes
patterns.example: for id in ...; do bosun ledger show "$id" | grep '"note"' | tail -1; done
patterns.protocol: ledger reports [--since]

patterns.name: my directives to the orchestrator
patterns.detail: delegate 4 ('delegate this to a sub-agent', 'spawn a sub agent', 'after it finishes its current round'), approve or reject proposals 4 ('send the Slack message', 'send it as written', 'no need, mark it done'), addendum 1, look-ups 2 ('see if we addressed this already'), draft from a session's result 1, re-read policy 2, chat 2 (a date question; a message meant for another window and its retraction)
patterns.protocol: delegations and addenda map to delegate and delegate --update; drafts come from reports

patterns.name: proposals and approvals
patterns.detail: 11 proposed; 6 done, 3 withdrawn (2 superseded, 1 already done elsewhere), 1 rejected, 1 pending
patterns.protocol: unchanged

patterns.name: messages about no work item
patterns.detail: chores commands 9 and drain prompts 3 to the orchestrator; drain and restart notices 14 to repo sessions; 2 notes from my other session to repo sessions (AWS credentials, session moved); 2 policy re-reads to the orchestrator; 3 interrupts. None came from the orchestrator itself, but they show itemless messages are legitimate
patterns.protocol: send --no-item for the orchestrator; internal callers and my own sends are unchanged

patterns.name: duplicate or overlapping work
patterns.detail: a review request proposed after the repo session had already posted it; two fix-my-pr tasks for PRs the session's own agents were already fixing ('already covered by the agents running on those PRs')
patterns.protocol: delegate refuses a second hand-over while the first awaits a report (--again after my approval), and list shows which window works on each item; work a session starts on its own is still invisible

patterns.name: delegated review with no outcome recorded
patterns.detail: both PRs were already approved; one session said so only in its window, the other was interrupted
patterns.protocol: report --state dismissed; list shows 'awaiting report'; delegate --update asks for one

patterns.name: delegated to another window than proposed
patterns.detail: two investigations proposed for exporter-tax went to exporter because the first was busy; only a note said so
patterns.protocol: the recorded delegation names the window actually used; delegate --update <id> --window <window> moves an item (whole task to the new window, a stop notice to the old one, the move recorded)

patterns.name: window start reported but not started
patterns.detail: day 1 09:39 send --new; fixed the same day (send exits non-zero)
patterns.protocol: a delegation is recorded only after send exits 0
patterns.not_covered: fixed before this corpus; covered by smoke tests of send --new

patterns.name: orchestrator shell slips
patterns.detail: `L="bosun ledger"; $L upsert ...` does not split under zsh (nothing written); `bosun ledger proposals` does not exist
patterns.protocol: unchanged (the CLI refuses unknown commands)

patterns.name: orchestrator stalled at a permission prompt
patterns.detail: a `gh api` read asked for approval at night; check-ins were skipped for about 14 hours
patterns.protocol: out of scope here (policy: never use gh api for reads; the watchdog work covers alerts)

patterns.name: work waiting on someone else's answer
patterns.detail: day 2 (later sessions): four product decisions deferred to a stakeholder at the end of a PR's work, kept in chat, PR text and a Slack reply while the mention that started it was marked done; a draft PR choosing between sending a due date and having another team's connector compute it, with 'note it for the other team' only in chat; a proposed Slack reply that asked the stakeholder back, with nothing recording that we then waited (their answer would have become a new mention); a session asking me twice whether to address bot reviews now or wait for the human reviewers
patterns.protocol: outreach items (out:<parent>/<n>): ledger reach-out/ask in draft, propose (-> proposed), sent with the message ref (follow-ups counted as nudges), replied with evidence, delegate --update <out-id> to the parent's window (-> applied); ledger seen names the outreach for messages in its Slack thread or DM; a parent with open outreach is not finished without --force-open-outreach. Questions for me stay in the report's open points

patterns.name: things recorded after they happened
patterns.detail: day 2: seven outreach messages (decisions a repo session posted in a Slack thread the day before, a DM it sent that morning, two decisions posted two hours earlier) were backfilled at one moment and all carried the recording time, so the nudge clock started up to a day late. Also seen, with the real time only in the note: PR merges, approvals and change requests recorded 1 to 16 hours after they happened, and Slack posts by a repo session recorded at the next check-in
patterns.protocol: ledger sent/replied take the time from --at (ISO 8601 with an offset, or local 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM'; never the future), else from a Slack permalink's own ts, else now; sent --at with a ref already recorded corrects its time; the history keeps the recording time with happened_at and time_from; the wait counts from the latest message time. State-change times stay in notes (ROADMAP)

patterns.name: overlapping outreach
patterns.detail: day 2: a repo session recorded five drafts within an hour: two to the same person about one log that grows without bound; an addition to a decision already sent in a Slack thread, as a second item waiting in that thread (`ledger seen` credited a reply there to the first item in ledger order); an FYI with no reply expected, which would have waited and been nudged forever. The check-in sent one nudge covering four sent items and recorded it on one, so the other three kept their old wait clocks
patterns.protocol: reach-out warns (does not refuse) when the parent has open outreach to the same person, naming it; an addition goes out as a follow-up on the existing item (ledger sent <existing id>) and the draft is folded into it (ledger fold <draft id> --into <existing id>, recording folded_into); upsert --field subject=/options= keeps the record in line with the message (title and subject are one); purpose fyi is one-way, sent -> applied at once; sent <id> [<id> ...] records one message on each item it covers; ledger seen names every open item sharing the thread, latest message first

patterns.name: work we decided to do, with no item of its own
patterns.detail: day 2: a colleague answered my PR's outreach with 'yes please fix' the same bug in the PDF renderer; the orchestrator proposed delegating new work under the outreach id. Before that was approved I asked the repo window directly, its session opened a new draft PR, and the orchestrator closed the outreach with a note naming the PR, which withdrew the proposal: the new PR had no ledger item. A Jira ticket assigned to me tracked the original PR, with nothing in the ledger about it; another PR carried its origin only as a free-form field
patterns.protocol: task items (task:<date>/<n>) spawned from the item that asked (ledger spawn, spawned_from with the reply as via), accepted only with 'user:' evidence, delegated under their own id; delegate refuses an outreach id as the work item; closing a replied outreach with no task prints the spawn command; reports print the commands that record and link a PR (produces); tickets (jira:<KEY>-<n>) are linked with tracks and mirrored read-only with ticket-sync, mismatches proposed; ledger migrate-links moves origin fields into spawned_from
